quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #24
										  					
  

35 Questions • Passing Score 28

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should:

options.text: Only use your mirrors.
Signal as you move into the next lane.
Signal at least 500 feet before changing lanes on residential streets.
Always check your blind spot.

questions.explanation: Cars and motorcycles can hide in your blind spot. Look over your shoulder before changing lanes. Signal 100 feet ahead on residential streets or 5 seconds ahead on freeways.

questions.question: How far ahead should you look while driving?

options.text: 10 seconds ahead
2 seconds ahead
As far ahead as possible
5 seconds ahead

questions.explanation: Look as far down the road as you can. This helps you spot problems early and avoid sudden moves.

questions.question: You turn left from a two-way street onto a one-way street. After the turn, your car should be:

options.text: In the right lane.
In the center of the street.
In the left lane.
In the lane with the least traffic.

questions.explanation: When turning left onto a one-way street, complete your turn into the lane closest to where you came from.

questions.question: You turn onto a two-lane road with a broken yellow line down the center. This tells you:

options.text: Traffic moves in opposite directions.
Traffic moves in one direction only.
The road is being repaired.
You must stay to the left of the broken line.

questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. Broken lines mean you can pass when safe.

questions.question: If an oncoming car uses high beams, look toward ____ of the road.

options.text: Either side
The center
The right side
The left side

questions.explanation: Look to the right side of the road. This keeps you from being blinded and helps you stay on course until the car passes.

questions.question: What happens if you crash without liability insurance?

options.text: You will be fined $50.
Your license will be revoked for six months.
Your license will be suspended for one year.
You will be fined $100.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your license will be suspended for one year.
questions.explanation: If you crash without proper insurance, your license will be suspended for one year.

questions.question: If you need to stop quickly and your car does not have Anti-Lock Brakes (ABS), you should:

options.text: Press and hold the brake pedal.
Pump the brakes firmly.
Tap the brakes lightly.
Release the brake pedal.

questions.explanation: Pumping the brakes is the best way to stop in an emergency. Your car will stop quickly and you can still steer.

questions.question: A single broken yellow line in the center of a two-lane road means:

options.text: Traffic moves in opposite directions and passing is not allowed.
Traffic moves in opposite directions and passing is allowed when safe.
Traffic moves in the same direction and passing is not allowed.
Traffic moves in the same direction and passing is allowed when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic moves in opposite directions and passing is allowed when safe.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. A broken line means you can pass when it is safe to do so.

questions.question: Can you turn left onto a one-way street at a red light?

options.text: Only if a left turn sign is posted.
Only if there is a green arrow.
Never.
Yes, if traffic allows.

questions.explanation: You can turn left or right onto a one-way street at a red light if you stop first and yield to all traffic and pedestrians. Check for signs that prohibit turns on red.

questions.question: When driving to a new area, you should:

options.text: Follow road signs to find your way.
Plan your trip before you start.
Only know generally where you are going.
Always take the most direct route.

questions.correctAnswerText: Plan your trip before you start.
questions.explanation: Plan your trip in advance. Check your destination on a map before you drive so you know where you are going.

questions.question: Traffic signals sometimes show arrows to control turns from specific lanes. What does a solid red arrow mean?

options.text: It is never used as a traffic signal.
It means the same thing as a red traffic light.
It means you can turn in the direction the arrow points.
It means traffic must stop in the direction the arrow points.

questions.correctAnswerText: It means the same thing as a red traffic light.
questions.explanation: A solid red arrow means the same thing as a red traffic light. You must stop and cannot turn in the direction the arrow points.

questions.question: What should you do when you approach a railroad crossing with no traffic signals?

options.text: Always come to a complete stop.
Slow down and be ready to stop.
All railroad crossings have signals, so this will never happen.
Speed up to cross the tracks quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: Slow down when you approach an unmarked railroad crossing and be ready to stop. Look both ways on all tracks before crossing. If you see or hear a train, stop at a safe distance and wait until the train passes.

questions.question: When is a road most likely to be slippery?

options.text: When it has deep, fresh snow.
When it is icy and very cold below freezing.
When it is icy and the temperature is near freezing.
When it is very cold and dry.

questions.correctAnswerText: When it is icy and the temperature is near freezing.
questions.explanation: Roads are most slippery when they are icy and the temperature is at or near freezing.

questions.question: When driving 30 mph or slower on normal roads, how far should you stay behind the car in front of you?

options.text: One second
Five seconds
Six seconds
Two seconds

questions.explanation: Keep two to four seconds between you and the car in front when driving 30 mph or slower. Use at least four seconds when driving faster on normal roads.

questions.question: When you park uphill on a street with a curb, what should you do with your wheels?

options.text: Keep them straight and set the parking brake.
Turn them away from the curb.
Turn them toward the curb.
Turn the back wheels into the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn them away from the curb.
questions.explanation: Turn your wheels away from the curb when parking uphill. This way, if your brakes fail, your car will roll into the curb instead of into traffic.

questions.question: When driving in bad weather, what should drivers do?

options.text: Drive faster to reach their destination sooner.
Follow closer to other vehicles.
Stay farther behind other vehicles.
None of the above.

questions.explanation: In bad weather and on wet roads, increase the distance between you and the car in front of you.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Keep right.
Keep left.
Pass with caution.
No passing.

questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a divided highway is ahead. The road will split into two one-way roads with a median between them. You must stay in the right lane.

questions.question: Traffic signals sometimes show arrows to control turns from specific lanes. What does a solid yellow arrow mean?

options.text: It is never used as a traffic signal.
It means the same thing as a yellow traffic light.
It means you can turn in the direction the arrow points.
It tells you a green arrow is coming next.

questions.correctAnswerText: It means the same thing as a yellow traffic light.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow arrow means the same thing as a yellow traffic light. Slow down and get ready to stop when you see it.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Steep downgrade.
Crossroad ahead.
No right turn.
Narrow bridge.

questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign tells you a steep hill is coming. Adjust your speed to protect your brakes and avoid crashes.

questions.question: Which of these does NOT affect how far your car travels before stopping?

options.text: Your reaction time.
The time of day.
The condition of your brakes.
The condition and type of your tires.

questions.explanation: Stopping distance depends on your reaction time, weather, road conditions, vehicle weight, brake condition, tire condition, and speed. The time of day does not affect stopping distance.

questions.question: A red flashing traffic light means the same thing as a:

options.text: Solid red light.
Stop sign.
Yield sign.
Caution sign.

questions.explanation: A red flashing traffic light means the same thing as a stop sign. You must come to a complete stop and then proceed when it is safe.

questions.question: A work zone:

options.text: Can be moving or stationary.
Is marked with black and white signs.
Does not require you to slow down and pay extra attention.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Work zones can be stationary or moving, such as vehicles striping lines, mowing, or removing snow. Work zones are marked with orange signs with black letters or symbols. Always slow down and pay close attention in work zones.

questions.question: Roads become very slippery:

options.text: When it has been raining for an hour or more.
The day after it rains.
During the first 10 to 15 minutes of a rainstorm.
Right after the rain stops.

questions.correctAnswerText: During the first 10 to 15 minutes of a rainstorm.
questions.explanation: Roads become very slippery at the start of rain because water brings oil from the road surface up to the top. This is even worse in hot weather because heat causes more oil to rise.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Crossroad ahead.
Flagger ahead.
Lane ends.
Turn right or go straight.

questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings and alert you to hazards ahead. This sign tells you an intersection is coming.

questions.question: Which statement about right-of-way at an unmarked T intersection is true?

options.text: Traffic on the road that ends has the right-of-way.
All traffic must stop. The driver who stopped first has the right-of-way.
All traffic must stop. The driver on the right has the right-of-way.
Traffic on the through-road has the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic on the through-road has the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: At an unmarked T intersection, traffic on the road that ends must yield to traffic on the through-road.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Hunting area.
State park.
Deer crossing.
Wildlife preserve.

questions.explanation: This sign warns that deer cross the road in this area. Slow down, stay alert, and be ready to stop.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Roundabout ahead.
No passing zone.
Left turn yield on green.
Traffic signal ahead.

questions.explanation: This sign tells you a traffic light is coming. Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.question: When entering a highway from an entrance ramp, you should:

options.text: Speed up faster than traffic to get ahead.
Enter slowly to avoid other vehicles.
Stop first, then slowly enter traffic.
Speed up to match the traffic speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up to match the traffic speed.
questions.explanation: Use the acceleration lane to speed up to match traffic speed. Signal, look for an opening, accelerate, and merge safely into traffic.

questions.question: What is a "No zone?"

options.text: A designated no passing zone.
A one-way traffic area.
The blind spot of a large vehicle.
An area designated for motor vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: The blind spot of a large vehicle.
questions.explanation: "No zones" are large blind spots around trucks and big vehicles. Avoid staying in these areas.

questions.question: When you see or hear an emergency vehicle coming, you should:

options.text: Stop right away and let it pass.
Drive to the right side of the road and stop.
Slow down and let the vehicle pass.
Keep moving slowly on the right side.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive to the right side of the road and stop.
questions.explanation: When you see or hear an emergency vehicle with lights or sirens, move to the right side of the road as far as safely possible and stop. Do not stop in an intersection.

questions.question: You see a flashing yellow light at an intersection. What should you do?

options.text: Stop and wait for the light to change.
Make a U-turn because the intersection is closed.
Drive carefully through the intersection.
Prepare to stop; the light is about to turn red.

questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means go slowly and look both ways before crossing. Check for traffic in all directions.

questions.question: What does drinking coffee do after you drink alcohol?

options.text: Decreases blood alcohol concentration.
Cancels the effect of the alcohol.
Has no effect on blood alcohol concentration.
Increases blood alcohol concentration.

questions.correctAnswerText: Has no effect on blood alcohol concentration.
questions.explanation: Coffee cannot lower your blood alcohol level. It may keep you awake, but it does not make you sober.

questions.question: How can you check your blind spots when changing lanes?

options.text: Using the inside rearview mirror.
Using the outside rearview mirror.
Using both inside and outside rearview mirrors.
Turning your head and looking over your shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turning your head and looking over your shoulder.
questions.explanation: Turn your head to look over your shoulder before every lane change. This is the only way to see your blind spots.

questions.question: When visibility is reduced, what should you do first?

options.text: Turning on your headlights.
Reducing your speed.
Turning on your windshield wipers.
Looking for road edge markings to guide you.

questions.explanation: Slow down first when visibility is poor. This is your most important response to unsafe road conditions.

questions.question: When merging onto a freeway, what is the best thing to do?

options.text: Proceed slowly while waiting for an opening.
Accelerate to a speed that is faster than the speed of traffic.
Turn on your hazard lights until safely on the freeway.
Accelerate to the speed of freeway traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Accelerate to the speed of freeway traffic.
questions.explanation: Speed up on the ramp to match freeway traffic speed. This helps you merge smoothly and safely. Vehicles entering must yield to cars already on the freeway.
